title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes the previous page's set-up. That page defined a relative MD-curve (Mumford–Deligne curve) over a base S as a proper flat curve with a set I of sections. Each geometric fibre must be a connected nodal curve whose nodes lie off the marked points. The fibres must also satisfy infinitesimal rigidity: no smooth genus-1 fibre without marks, and every genus-0 component carries 'marked weight' (special points) at least 3. In modern terms this is a stable ν-pointed curve.

First sentence. The numerical type (g,ν) is a locally constant function on S. Here g comes from χ(O) of the fibres and ν = card I_s. This holds even though the combinatorial (dual-graph) type of the fibres may jump.

Next, fix an 'anabelian' numerical type, 2g+ν ≥ 3, equivalently 2g−2+ν > 0, the hyperbolic or stable range. Grothendieck considers the fibred groupoid (eq. 24) S ↦ \hat M_{g,ν}(S), the groupoid of relative MD-curves over S of type (g,ν).

'Mumford–Deligne theorem': this fibred groupoid over (Sch), or more generally over schematic multiplicities, is representable by a schematic multiplicity \hat M_{g,ν} that is smooth and proper over Spec Z. In modern language, the moduli stack \bar M_{g,n} of stable n-pointed genus-g curves is a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack over Z.

A crossed-out start ('D'autre part M_{g,ν} ...') is resumed on the next page. There M_{g,ν} is an open dense substack, fibrewise schematically dense. Connectedness of the geometric fibres in all characteristics follows from characteristic 0. Strata M_{[G]} indexed by MD-graph types immerse into \hat M_{g,ν}. These notes prepare the study of the 'structure at infinity' (the boundary stratification) of the M_{g,ν}, in connection with the Teichmüller tower and anabelian geometry.
errors: Attribution: for ν>0 the theorem is due to Knudsen (1983, 'The projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves II/III'), building on Deligne–Mumford 1969 for ν=0. Grothendieck's label 'Mumford-Deligne' omits Knudsen; this is historical, not mathematical.
Otherwise the statement is correct: 2g+ν≥3 is exactly the stability condition 2g−2+ν>0, and \bar M_{g,n} is smooth and proper over Spec Z as a DM stack.

deep.surprise_reason: The page restates the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen theorem in Grothendieck's idiosyncratic terminology. It is enthusiastic ('vraiment magnifique') but contains nothing beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: The equation label appears to be (24), not (21); this is consistent with the next page's (25).
The margin insertion reads 'On suppose 2g+ν≥3 (cas anabélien)'.
The struck-out final line begins 'D'autre part M_{g,ν} est un ...'. The crossed words are hard to read; the next page shows the intended continuation was 'ouvert de Zariski de \hat M_{g,ν}'.
